title: Ozempic price in November 2026, and how to get a prescription
summary: Ozempic price Nov 2026: Novo Nordisk self-pay pen $199 to $499/mo, pill $149 to $299, as little as $25 with commercial coverage. How to get a prescription.
body_markdown:
Getting Ozempic (semaglutide) requires a prescription from a licensed health care provider ([NovoCare](https://www.novocare.com/delivery/ozempic.html) ), and every indication on its FDA label is for adults with type 2 diabetes. Through[NovoCare](https://www.novocare.com/delivery/ozempic.html) in November 2026, Novo Nordisk's self-pay pen is $199 a month for two starter fills (0.25 or 0.5 mg, through December 31, 2026), then $349, or $499 for 2 mg; the pill is $149 to $299. With commercial coverage, the[savings card](https://www.ozempic.com/savings-and-resources/save-on-ozempic.html) lowers the pen to as little as $25 a month. A FutureClinic physician visit by message is $40.


## How do you get an Ozempic prescription online?


You get an Ozempic prescription by discussing your health history and current medicines with a licensed health care provider ([NovoCare](https://www.novocare.com/delivery/ozempic.html) ). Both the[pen label](https://www.novo-pi.com/ozempic.pdf) and[tablet label](https://www.novo-pi.com/ozempictablets.pdf) carry a boxed warning for rodent thyroid C-cell tumors: a personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma (MTC), or having Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia syndrome type 2 (MEN 2) rules Ozempic out.


Under the[FDA label](https://www.novo-pi.com/ozempic.pdf) , weekly pens start at 0.25 mg for four weeks, move to 0.5 mg, and can step up to 1 mg and 2 mg for glucose control, each after at least four weeks. Daily[tablets](https://www.novo-pi.com/ozempictablets.pdf) come in 1.5 mg, 4 mg, and 9 mg doses ([ozempic.com](https://www.ozempic.com/) ).

## Who can prescribe Ozempic, and is it approved for weight loss?


Any licensed health care provider who prescribes can write an Ozempic prescription after reviewing your health history and goals ([NovoCare](https://www.novocare.com/delivery/ozempic.html) ), and its[FDA label](https://www.novo-pi.com/ozempic.pdf) covers only adults with type 2 diabetes. On FutureClinic, you always see a physician (MD, DO or MBBS). Its[FDA label](https://www.novo-pi.com/ozempic.pdf) covers glycemic control and reducing major cardiovascular events or kidney decline in adults with type 2 diabetes and established heart or kidney disease. The[American Diabetes Association](https://diabetes.org/about-diabetes/diagnosis) diagnoses diabetes at an A1C of 6.5% or higher, usually confirmed on a second day (prediabetes is 5.7% to 6.4%); no fasting is needed.


According to[healthinsurance.org](https://www.healthinsurance.org/faqs/does-health-insurance-cover-drugs-used-for-weight-loss-such-as-ozempic-wegovy-mounjaro-and-zepbound/) (August 20, 2026), Wegovy, Zepbound, Saxenda, and Foundayo hold FDA approval for weight management, while Ozempic does not. According to the[FDA](https://www.fda.gov/patients/learn-about-expanded-access-and-other-treatment-options/understanding-unapproved-use-approved-drugs-label) , clinicians generally may prescribe a drug off-label when they judge it medically appropriate, yet Wegovy has the same active ingredient, semaglutide ([Ro](https://ro.co/weight-loss/) ), and[coverage for weight loss alone is much less common](https://www.healthinsurance.org/faqs/does-health-insurance-cover-drugs-used-for-weight-loss-such-as-ozempic-wegovy-mounjaro-and-zepbound/) .[When weight is the goal](https://futureclinic.com/blog/weight-loss-medication-online-no-membership-fee) without diabetes, a doctor may discuss[Wegovy or Zepbound](https://futureclinic.com/blog/zepbound-or-wegovy-online-without-a-membership) , which are FDA-approved for chronic weight management ([healthinsurance.org](https://www.healthinsurance.org/faqs/does-health-insurance-cover-drugs-used-for-weight-loss-such-as-ozempic-wegovy-mounjaro-and-zepbound/) ).


## What does Ozempic cost without insurance in November 2026?


Without insurance, Novo Nordisk's self-pay Ozempic price is $199 (new patients' first two fills) to $499 a month for the pen and $149 to $299 for the pill ([NovoCare](https://www.novocare.com/delivery/ozempic.html) , November 2026); without a coupon or program,[GoodRx](https://www.goodrx.com/ozempic) puts average retail for Ozempic's most common version at $1,212.42.


Route Price (Nov 2026) Source


Pen, new patients (0.25, 0.5 mg) $199/mo for 2 fills (to Dec 31, 2026) NovoCare, ozempic.com


Pen, ongoing self-pay (0.25, 0.5, 1 mg) $349/mo NovoCare, ozempic.com


Pen 2 mg, self-pay $499/mo NovoCare, ozempic.com


Pill, self-pay (30 tablets) $149 (1.5 mg), $199 (4 mg), $299 (9 mg)/mo (1.5 mg is the starting dose) GoodRx, NovoCare, tablet label


Commercial insurance + savings card As little as $25/mo (up to $100/mo off) NovoCare, ozempic.com


Average retail, most common version (no coupon) $1,212.42 GoodRx


Prices checked on November 23, 2026.


Commercial plans commonly cover Ozempic for type 2 diabetes ([healthinsurance.org](https://www.healthinsurance.org/faqs/does-health-insurance-cover-drugs-used-for-weight-loss-such-as-ozempic-wegovy-mounjaro-and-zepbound/) ), sometimes with prior authorization ([ozempic.com](https://www.ozempic.com/savings-and-resources/save-on-ozempic.html) ), and much less often for weight loss alone ([healthinsurance.org](https://www.healthinsurance.org/faqs/does-health-insurance-cover-drugs-used-for-weight-loss-such-as-ozempic-wegovy-mounjaro-and-zepbound/) ). The[savings card](https://www.ozempic.com/savings-and-resources/save-on-ozempic.html) drops commercial pen copays to as little as $25 a month (up to $100 off a month, for up to 48 months). Most Medicare Part D plans cover Ozempic for diabetes ([ozempic.com](https://www.ozempic.com/savings-and-resources/save-on-ozempic.html) ), not weight loss ([healthinsurance.org](https://www.healthinsurance.org/faqs/does-health-insurance-cover-drugs-used-for-weight-loss-such-as-ozempic-wegovy-mounjaro-and-zepbound/) ); Part D members cannot use the $25 card, though they are eligible for self-pay options ([ozempic.com](https://www.ozempic.com/savings-and-resources/save-on-ozempic.html) ). Self-pay does not count toward deductibles ([NovoCare](https://www.novocare.com/delivery/ozempic.html) ), and no generic exists ([GoodRx](https://www.goodrx.com/ozempic) ). Starting January 2027, Novo Nordisk cuts the list price 35% to $675 a month ([CBS News](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/wegovy-ozempic-novo-nordisk-price-cut-january-2027/) ), and in January 2027 a $274 Medicare negotiated price for semaglutide takes effect;[KFF](https://www.kff.org/quick-insights/understanding-the-trump-administrations-negotiated-drug-prices-for-medicare/) notes it's unclear how it will interact with a $245 Medicare price from a Trump administration deal. To pay less today, use the $199 starter offer, ask your physician whether the[4 mg pill](https://www.novo-pi.com/ozempictablets.pdf) ([$199](https://www.goodrx.com/ozempic) ) fits, or let FutureClinic help with prior authorization so you can use your plan and the $25 savings card.
